item.title: Eclipse C++11/14/17 Support: Resolving Undefined Symbols & Compiler Flags
item.description:
“Eclipse C++11/14/17 Support: Resolving Undefined Symbols & Compiler Flags”

Encountering issues with undefined symbols like std::thread or std::unique_ptr within Eclipse CDT for C++11, C++14, or C++17 projects can be frustrating. These problems often stem from the IDE’s indexer not being aware of the C++ standard being used by the compiler. This can lead to apparent errors in the editor even when the code compiles and runs successfully from the command line. This post explores various methods to configure Eclipse CDT to correctly recognize and support modern C++ standards, ensuring your IDE accurately reflects your build environment.

item.title: Fixing Eclipse ADT Plugin Conflicts: Solutions for Version Upgrade Issues
item.description:
“Fixing Eclipse ADT Plugin Conflicts: Solutions for Version Upgrade Issues”

When attempting to upgrade the Android Development Tools (ADT) plugin within the Eclipse IDE, users frequently encounter issues, particularly concerning conflicting dependencies when moving to versions like 23.0.2. This situation arises because the upgrade process struggles to reconcile old components with the new installation requirements. Here are several established procedures to navigate this complex environment and restore development capability.

Scenarios and Remedial Actions for ADT Upgrade Failures

The recommended paths depend heavily on whether you used the standalone ADT Bundle or installed the ADT plugin manually into an existing Eclipse installation.

item.title: Fix javax servlet http HttpServlet Not Found in Eclipse
item.description:
“Fix javax servlet http HttpServlet Not Found in Eclipse”

Encountering the “The superclass ‘javax.servlet.http.HttpServlet’ was not found on the Java Build Path” error in Eclipse can be a common hurdle when developing Java web applications. This typically arises when your project’s build path is not correctly configured to include the necessary Servlet API libraries provided by your application server. Let’s explore the various reasons and solutions for this pervasive issue.
